title: Digestion, Molecules, and Cell Fuel Core Test
description: Core practice for trace how digestive, circulatory, and cellular processes turn food into usable materials and energy access for cells.

questions.prompt: What does digestion do to large food molecules?
questions.questionText: What does digestion do to large food molecules?
options: breaks them into smaller molecules cells can use
questions.correctAnswer: breaks them into smaller molecules cells can use
questions.explanation: Digestion makes food materials usable.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best traces food to cells?
questions.questionText: Which sequence best traces food to cells?
options: cell -> fossil -> food label -> no transport
food -> digestion -> absorbed molecules -> blood transport -> cell use
questions.correctAnswer: food -> digestion -> absorbed molecules -> blood transport -> cell use
questions.explanation: The model connects systems.

questions.prompt: A cracker tastes sweeter after chewing. What is a reasonable explanation?
questions.questionText: A cracker tastes sweeter after chewing. What is a reasonable explanation?
options: the cracker becomes a living cell
starch begins breaking into smaller sugar molecules
questions.correctAnswer: starch begins breaking into smaller sugar molecules
questions.explanation: Chemical digestion can begin in the mouth.

questions.prompt: Which systems interact to deliver glucose to muscle cells?
questions.questionText: Which systems interact to deliver glucose to muscle cells?
questions.correctAnswer: digestive and circulatory systems
questions.explanation: Digestion absorbs; circulation transports.

questions.prompt: A student says the stomach gives energy directly to muscles. What is best?
questions.questionText: A student says the stomach gives energy directly to muscles. What is best?
options: Food molecules are broken down and transported before cells release usable energy.
The stomach sends whole food into muscles.
questions.correctAnswer: Food molecules are broken down and transported before cells release usable energy.
questions.explanation: Cells release usable energy from molecules.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would support digestion of starch?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would support digestion of starch?
options: a test shows starch decreases and smaller sugars increase over time
questions.correctAnswer: a test shows starch decreases and smaller sugars increase over time
questions.explanation: Chemical evidence can show breakdown.

questions.prompt: Why does blood matter in the model?
questions.questionText: Why does blood matter in the model?
options: it transports absorbed molecules to cells throughout the body
questions.correctAnswer: it transports absorbed molecules to cells throughout the body
questions.explanation: Blood connects organs to cells.

questions.prompt: What do active muscle cells usually need more of?
questions.questionText: What do active muscle cells usually need more of?
questions.correctAnswer: glucose and oxygen
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration uses glucose and oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which question pushes beyond recall?
questions.questionText: Which question pushes beyond recall?
options: How would cell demand change during exercise and why?
How many letters are in glucose?
questions.correctAnswer: How would cell demand change during exercise and why?
questions.explanation: It asks for transfer and cause/effect.

questions.prompt: Which model has a missing step?
questions.questionText: Which model has a missing step?
options: food -> muscle cell, with no digestion or transport shown
questions.correctAnswer: food -> muscle cell, with no digestion or transport shown
questions.explanation: The missing steps are the explanation.

questions.prompt: Food provides matter as well as energy-related molecules. Which evidence fits matter use?
questions.questionText: Food provides matter as well as energy-related molecules. Which evidence fits matter use?
options: amino acids from food are used to build body proteins
questions.correctAnswer: amino acids from food are used to build body proteins
questions.explanation: Food atoms can become body materials.

questions.prompt: What is cellular respiration?
questions.questionText: What is cellular respiration?
options: a cell process that releases usable energy from molecules such as glucose
questions.correctAnswer: a cell process that releases usable energy from molecules such as glucose
questions.explanation: Respiration is a cell-level chemical process.

questions.prompt: A runner breathes faster after sprinting. How does that connect?
questions.questionText: A runner breathes faster after sprinting. How does that connect?
options: muscle cells need more oxygen for cellular respiration
oxygen is a food web arrow
questions.correctAnswer: muscle cells need more oxygen for cellular respiration
questions.explanation: Breathing supports oxygen delivery.

questions.prompt: Which table would best test system interaction?
questions.questionText: Which table would best test system interaction?
options: food molecule, digestion product, blood transport, cell use
questions.correctAnswer: food molecule, digestion product, blood transport, cell use
questions.explanation: The table connects evidence across levels.

questions.prompt: Why is saying 'food turns into energy' too simple?
questions.questionText: Why is saying 'food turns into energy' too simple?
options: food molecules are matter, and cells transform energy during chemical reactions
questions.correctAnswer: food molecules are matter, and cells transform energy during chemical reactions
questions.explanation: The better explanation separates matter and energy.

questions.prompt: Which scenario best shows transfer?
questions.questionText: Which scenario best shows transfer?
options: drawing a plate with no labels
explaining how rice starch can become glucose delivered to cells
questions.correctAnswer: explaining how rice starch can become glucose delivered to cells
questions.explanation: It applies the model to a new food.

questions.prompt: A diagram ends at absorbed glucose in blood. What should be added?
questions.questionText: A diagram ends at absorbed glucose in blood. What should be added?
options: delivery to cells and use in cell processes
questions.correctAnswer: delivery to cells and use in cell processes
questions.explanation: The concept continues to cells.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern supports higher cell demand during activity?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern supports higher cell demand during activity?
options: heart and breathing rates rise during exercise and recover after rest
questions.correctAnswer: heart and breathing rates rise during exercise and recover after rest
questions.explanation: Body responses support increased delivery needs.

questions.prompt: What is the role of oxygen in this model?
questions.questionText: What is the role of oxygen in this model?
options: it is used with glucose in cellular respiration
questions.correctAnswer: it is used with glucose in cellular respiration
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a reactant in respiration.

questions.prompt: A student claims one body system works alone. Which evidence challenges it?
questions.questionText: A student claims one body system works alone. Which evidence challenges it?
options: digestion products appear in blood and are used by cells
questions.correctAnswer: digestion products appear in blood and are used by cells
questions.explanation: Evidence connects multiple systems.

questions.prompt: If absorption in the small intestine decreases, what cell-level effect is possible?
questions.questionText: If absorption in the small intestine decreases, what cell-level effect is possible?
questions.correctAnswer: fewer useful molecules reach cells
questions.explanation: Less absorption can reduce delivery.

questions.prompt: Which explanation handles both matter and energy?
questions.questionText: Which explanation handles both matter and energy?
options: Food is only a feeling of energy.
Food molecules provide atoms for building and glucose for cells to release usable energy.
questions.correctAnswer: Food molecules provide atoms for building and glucose for cells to release usable energy.
questions.explanation: This explains both roles.

questions.prompt: Why is chewing part of the model?
questions.questionText: Why is chewing part of the model?
options: it moves glucose through blood by itself
it increases breakdown and exposes food to digestive chemicals
questions.correctAnswer: it increases breakdown and exposes food to digestive chemicals
questions.explanation: Mechanical and chemical digestion can work together.

questions.prompt: Which final summary is best?
questions.questionText: Which final summary is best?
options: Digestion, circulation, and cells interact so food molecules become useful materials and fuel for cell processes.
Only the stomach gives all energy.
questions.correctAnswer: Digestion, circulation, and cells interact so food molecules become useful materials and fuel for cell processes.
questions.explanation: This connects systems and cells.

questions.prompt: What investigation could extend the cracker observation?
questions.questionText: What investigation could extend the cracker observation?

change food, time, and observer all at once

questions.explanation: Controlling variables makes the observation more useful.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best avoids memorizing only vocabulary?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best avoids memorizing only vocabulary?

It connects the model, evidence, and cause/effect relationship.

questions.prompt: Which type of evidence would make the claim stronger?
questions.questionText: Which type of evidence would make the claim stronger?
questions.correctAnswer: repeated observations under controlled conditions
questions.explanation: Repeated controlled observations strengthen claims.

questions.prompt: What should a careful scientist avoid?
questions.questionText: What should a careful scientist avoid?
options: changing several variables and then claiming one cause with certainty
questions.correctAnswer: changing several variables and then claiming one cause with certainty
questions.explanation: Fair tests protect conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which prompt asks for transfer?
questions.questionText: Which prompt asks for transfer?
